newsitem.title: USA: Goodyear shows 12 percent earnings growth.
newsitem.headline: Goodyear shows 12 percent earnings growth.

text.p: Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company Monday announced a 12 percent gain in first-quarter earnings, citing improved sales and productivity.
Net income for the period rose to $170.4 million, or $1.09 per share, from $151.8 million, or 98 cents per share, in the first quarter of 1996.
Sales for the quarter were $3.23 billion, compared with $3.25 billion in the 1996 quarter. The company said sales were adversely affected by the strong U.S. dollar and competitive pricing.
The company's worldwide tire unit sales in the quarter rose 3.6 percent over 1996 on increased volume in all regions.
In the United States, 1997 first-quarter sales were $1.71 billion, compared with $1.73 billion in 1996.
Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Samir G. Gibara attributed the overall growth to increased sales volumes and productivity programmes.

The earnings improvement reflected lower raw material costs and continued productivity gains, ongoing cost containment measures and restructuring activities. Both cost of goods sold and selling, administrative and general expenses decreased in dollars and as a percent of sales compared with the 1996 first quarter.
It was the company's 24th consecutive year-over-year quarterly gain, Goodyear said.

Goodyear had a $255 million improvement in operating cash flow over the 1996 first quarter. Global capital expenditures in the quarter, largely as a result of programme timing, were $94.4 million, compared with $127.9 million in the 1996 quarter.
Depreciation expense was $116.1 million, up from $111.6 million in the 1996 quarter.
Goodyear's stock lost 50 cents to $49.75 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
